## Project Overview

This research series explores the intersection of geography, economics, and institutional policy within the Roman Catholic Church in the United States. Utilizing a dataset of over 23,000 geolocated parishes combined with US Census data and AI-derived infrastructure footprints from Overture Maps, these papers analyze how legacy boundaries impact modern service delivery and urban land use.

### Research Papers

*   [**Canonical Rigidity & Sacred Space**](Canonical_Rigidity_Research_Paper.html)
    A spatial econometric analysis of how legacy territorial boundaries create "spatial leakage" and service inefficiencies.

*   [**Economics of Church Consolidation**](Economics_of_Church_Consolidation.html)
    Modeling market consolidation and identifying high-value real estate assets for potential redevelopment.

*   [**Sacred Spaces to Social Housing**](Closure_Conversion_Recommendations.html)
    A strategic analysis of converting underutilized urban church parking into multi-family residential housing.

*   [**Spiritual Landscapes**](Spiritual_Landscapes_Paper.html)
    A geospatial and demographic exploration of the Church's physical presence across the US.

---

*This project was developed using R (sf, tidyverse) and Python (Overture Maps API), rendered with Quarto.*
